amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي (19 مادة، بلا تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول) -- الموافقة على تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات السعودية، بعد الاطلاع على معاملة ديوان رئاسة مجلس الوزراء رقم (7/ب/4626) وتاريخ 4/3/1422هـ المشتملة على برقية وخطاب معالي وزير البرق والبريد والهاتف بشأن مشروعي نظام الاتصالات وتنظيم الهيئة، وقرار مجلس الشورى رقم (97/83) وتاريخ 19/2/1422هـ، وقرار المجلس الاقتصادي الأعلى رقم (2/22) وتاريخ 4/3/1422هـ. لم يُعثر على سلف تنظيمي مسمى لهذه الهيئة (هيئة مستقلة حديثة الإنشاء وقت صدور هذا القرار؛ قطاع الاتصالات كان يُدار مباشرة عبر وزارة البرق والبريد والهاتف).

إيكال مهمات تقنية المعلومات إلى هيئة الاتصالات، وتعديل مسمى الهيئة ليصبح (هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات)، مع تعديل تنظيمها بما يتلاءم والمسمى الجديد وإضافة مهمات تقنية المعلومات إلى مهماتها. أثّر على المادة الثالثة فقط (خطوة وسيطة استُبدلت بالكامل لاحقاً بموجب القرار 430). لم يتضمن نصاً صريحاً بتحديث تعريفات المادة الأولى للاسم الجديد (انظر cst_resolution133_and_253_renames_not_spliced_into_articles).

تعديل الفقرة (1) من المادة الرابعة (تشكيل مجلس الإدارة) -- رقم القرار ورد فارغاً في شعبة تعديلات المادة على موقع هيئة الخبراء بمجلس الوزراء ذاته، واستُكمل اعتماداً على مطابقته الحرفية الكاملة بين nezams.com وديباجة القرار 430. استُبدلت هذه الفقرة بالكامل لاحقاً بموجب القرار 430 (خطوة وسيطة).

(أ) إنشاء مجلس باسم (المجلس الأعلى للفضاء) برئاسة ولي العهد. (ب) تكليف المجلس الأعلى للفضاء وهيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات ورئيس مجلس إدارة الهيئة السعودية للفضاء بإعداد مشاريع تنظيمية تكميلية خلال 30 يوماً. (ج) إلغاء الفقرة (1) من البند (ثانياً) من قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (209) وتاريخ 25/4/1440هـ (الترتيبات التنظيمية للهيئة السعودية للفضاء -- تنظيم منفصل، غير مُدرج في هذا المسار). (د) البند (خامساً): 1- تعديل اسم (هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات) ليكون (هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية). 2- نقل الاختصاص التنظيمي والرقابي لقطاع الفضاء المدني من الهيئة السعودية للفضاء إلى هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية. لا يتضمن هذا القرار نصاً صريحاً يستبدل عبارات بعينها ضمن مواد تنظيم الهيئة الصادر بالقرار 74 (انظر cst_resolution133_and_253_renames_not_spliced_into_articles) -- BOE's own system_title/metadata reflects الاسم الجديد، لكن نص المادة الأولى التعريفي لم يُحدَّث نصياً.

تعديل شامل نُشر في جريدة أم القرى، العدد (5065)، الصادر في 17/1/2025م (17/7/1446هـ)، شمل: أولاً- المادة الأولى (حذف تعريف "النظام"، إضافة تعريف "القطاعات ذات الصلة بالهيئة"). ثانياً- المادة الثالثة (استبدال كامل، 26 اختصاصاً). ثالثاً- المادة الرابعة (استبدال كامل، مجلس إدارة من 7 أعضاء). رابعاً- المادة الخامسة (استبدال فقرتين (ب) و(ج)، حذف الفقرة (ط)، إضافة عجز جديد). خامساً- المادة الثامنة (إضافة ثلاث فقرات (ي)(ك)(ل)). سادساً- المادة العاشرة (استبدال كامل، 8 مصادر مالية) مع بند انتقالي عن استمرار المجلس القائم لحين تشكيل مجلس جديد وبند عن إقرار المقابلات المالية بالاتفاق مع وزارة المالية. BOE's own portal (Wayback 20260227062514) carries this resolution's own popup text VERBATIM for Articles 3 and 4 only; Articles 1, 5, 8 and 10's text for this resolution rests on qanoonsa.com's gazette reproduction alone (see verification_methodology_note and cst_boe_stale_no_popup_for_articles_1_5_8_10).

chapter_structure.label_ar: بدون تقسيم إلى أبواب أو فصول
chapter_structure.title_ar: مواد متسلسلة غير مجمعة تحت أبواب أو فصول رسمية، لا يحمل أي منها عنواناً فرعياً في المصدر: التعريفات (م1، معدّلة) -- إنشاء الهيئة وشخصيتها الاعتبارية ومقرها (م2) -- اختصاصات الهيئة، معدّلة بالكامل (26 اختصاصاً) (م3) -- تشكيل مجلس الإدارة، معدّل بالكامل (م4) -- اختصاصات مجلس الإدارة، معدّلة جزئياً (م5) -- اجتماعات المجلس وقراراته (م6) -- الاستعانة بالهيئات والمستشارين (م7) -- تعيين المحافظ واختصاصاته، مُضاف إليها ثلاث فقرات (م8) -- نواب المحافظ (م9) -- الموارد المالية للهيئة، معدّلة بالكامل (م10) -- إيداع أموال الهيئة (م11) -- تحصيل المقابل المالي (م12) -- الإعفاء الجمركي (م13) -- السنة المالية (م14) -- خضوع منسوبي الهيئة لنظامي العمل والتأمينات الاجتماعية (م15) -- التقرير السنوي (م16) -- مراجع الحسابات الخارجي ورقابة ديوان المراقبة العامة (م17) -- الإلغاء (م18) -- النشر والنفاذ (م19).

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS THIS PASS: laws.boe.gov.sa's LIVE portal was retried fresh this pass (curl over the pre-configured proxy, verbose TLS trace) and again returned a TLS connection reset during the handshake itself (CONNECT tunnel completed at HTTP 200, reset occurred during the TLS ClientHello/handshake, not a proxy-side denial) -- consistent with the prior research pass's finding that laws.boe.gov.sa is blocked/reset. UNLIKE that prior pass, however, the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) WAS fully reachable this pass via direct curl (HTTPS, following redirects) -- no egress-policy block and no TLS reset were encountered against web.archive.org itself this time. This track therefore rests PRIMARILY on two Wayback Machine captures of laws.boe.gov.sa's own 'LawDetails' page for this statute (Id f327464b-2f5a-475d-aa94-a9a700f2e817), located via a WebSearch query that surfaced the exact BOE Law ID (the search snippet itself named the law 'تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات', the pre-2022 name, confirming the same BOE law record has been updated in place across all three historical names rather than re-issued under a new Id):
  (1) capture timestamp 20250211150515 (11 Feb 2025) -- captured AFTER Resolution 430 (24 Dec 2024G/23 Jumada II 1446H) but shows NO trace of it (no '430', no '253', no 'الفضاء' anywhere in the page, and the system_title still reads the pre-2022 CITC name) -- i.e. BOE's own database had not yet been updated with either the 2022 rename or the 2024 restructuring as of this snapshot date, even though both decrees already existed by then. This snapshot's 19 articles were used as one cross-check point for the pristine 2001 original text.
  (2) capture timestamp 20260227062514 (27 Feb 2026, the most recent snapshot the Wayback CDX index has for this URL) -- this snapshot's system_title and page-title HAVE been updated to 'تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية' (the current CST name), its system_details summary paragraph explicitly cites 'قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (253) وتاريخ 1444/4/7هـ' as the renaming decree, and its own per-article amendment-history popups ('تعديلات المادة') for Article 3 and Article 4 explicitly quote 'قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (430) وتاريخ 1446/6/23هـ' with the FULL replacement text of both articles. This is a genuine, confirmed instance of BOE's own database catching up between two Wayback captures -- NOT a case of picking a more convenient secondary source; the Feb 2026 snapshot IS BOE's own official portal content, cached by the Wayback Machine.

CRITICAL FINDING -- BOE's Article-level amendment popups remain INCOMPLETE even in the Feb 2026 snapshot: BOE's own page carries a 'تعديلات المادة' (article amendments) popup ONLY for Article 3 and Article 4 (Resolution 430's full replacement text for both, plus Article 4's earlier Resolution 120 entry with its own decree NUMBER FIELD LEFT BLANK -- the popup's own text reads literally 'بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم () وتاريخ 1440/2/21هـ', an empty pair of parentheses where the number should be. This gap was filled by cross-checking nezams.com (which independently states the number as '(120)' with byte-for-byte identical replacement text) and qanoonsa.com's own reproduction of Resolution 430, whose recital independently lists 'قرارات مجلس الوزراء رقم (120) وتاريخ 21/2/1440هـ' among the resolutions it supersedes -- both agree on '120', so this track uses that number with the gap explicitly flagged, not silently filled.). NO popup exists on BOE's own page for Articles 1, 5, 8, or 10, despite qanoonsa.com's full reproduction of Resolution 430 explicitly stating that all four of these articles were ALSO amended by the same Resolution 430. This means BOE's own database is confirmed STALE for these four specific articles' amendment history as of the most recent snapshot available -- a genuine, confirmed limitation of the primary source, not an oversight of this research pass (the popups for Articles 1, 5, 8, 10 were searched for specifically and confirmed absent, both via a class-based BeautifulSoup parse of every article_item div and via raw-text occurrence counting of each article's own heading string).

SECONDARY CROSS-CHECK -- qanoonsa.com (https://qanoonsa.com/p/506510/): this page reproduces the COMPLETE text of Council of Ministers Resolution No. (430), dated 23 Jumada al-Thani 1446H (24 December 2024G), including its full recital chain (citing the Royal Diwan referral, the Ministry of Communications and IT's own memo, Royal Order 55685/30-11-1438H, the base Resolution 74/5-3-1422H, prior Resolutions 120/1440H, 524/11-9-1443H, 681/29-11-1443H, and 253/7-4-1444H, four numbered Experts' Commission memoranda, an Economic Affairs Council minute, and the General Committee of the Council of Ministers' recommendation), its full operative text amending Articles 1, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 10 verbatim, the King's signature line, and the exact Umm Al-Qura Gazette issue number (5065, published 17 Jan 2025). For Articles 3 and 4, qanoonsa's text was diffed programmatically against BOE's own popup text and found to be a WORD-FOR-WORD match (both reproduce the identical 26-item Article 3 and 7-member Article 4). This exact match across an independent aggregator and BOE's own portal is treated as strong corroboration that qanoonsa's reproduction of the REMAINING Articles 1, 5, 8, 10 amendment text (which BOE itself does not yet carry) is equally faithful to the gazette -- but it remains, honestly, a SINGLE-SOURCE reliance for those four articles' 2024 amendment layer specifically, since no second source (BOE included) currently carries that text. qanoonsa.com's separate page (https://qanoonsa.com/p/495610/) similarly reproduces the complete text of Resolution No. (253), dated 7/4/1444H (1 Nov 2022G) -- this resolution (a) creates a new 'Supreme Space Council', (b) tasks it and the Saudi Space Agency's board with drafting their own follow-on organizing instruments within 30 days, (c) repeals one paragraph of the Space Agency's own separate arrangements (Resolution 209/25-4-1440H, a DIFFERENT authority's statute, not ingested by this track), and (d) in its item 'خامساً' RENAMES 'هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات' to 'هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية' and transfers civil-space regulatory authority to it from the Space Agency. Critically, Resolution 253's own text does NOT contain an explicit 'wherever the phrase X appears in [this statute], substitute Y' instruction directed at the numbered articles of Resolution 74's organizing statute -- it is a broader naming/mandate decision, not a textual amendment to a specific article. This explains, and is consistent with, BOE's own page: the LAW'S OWN metadata/title updated to the new name, but Article 1's own definitions of 'الهيئة'/'التنظيم'/'المجلس'/'المحافظ'/'العضو' were NOT textually re-spliced and still read 'هيئة الاتصالات السعودية' verbatim (the ORIGINAL 2001 name, not even the intermediate 2003 CITC name) -- see cst_article1_entity_name_not_updated_despite_two_renames below.

TRIPLE CROSS-CHECK OF THE BASE (2001) TEXT -- nezams.com (https://nezams.com/تنظيم-هيئة-الاتصالات-السعودية/, fetched directly via curl with a browser User-Agent after an initial 406 from a bare request) independently reproduces the full 19-article original text, including the Resolution 120 amendment note to Article 4 (with the decree number '120' explicit, filling BOE's own blank). A full word-for-word diff of all 19 articles' original/unamended text across (a) BOE Wayback snapshot 20250211150515, (b) BOE Wayback snapshot 20260227062514, and (c) nezams.com found NO discrepancies -- the three sources are byte-for-byte identical on every unamended article and on the recital/preamble text. nezams.com's own page metadata states 'التعديلات: لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' (no amendments recorded) except the Resolution-120 note buried in Article 4's own text -- i.e. nezams.com has NOT been updated to reflect either Resolution 253 or Resolution 430 at all, and must not be read as corroborating (or contradicting) either of those two later amendments; it corroborates ONLY the base text and Resolution 120.

OTHER SOURCES ATTEMPTED: cst.gov.sa (the Commission's own site) returned a TLS connection reset identical in signature to laws.boe.gov.sa's (CONNECT tunnel completed, reset during the TLS handshake) -- confirmed unreachable this pass, not merely unattempted. argaam.com's linked article confirms only that the Council of Ministers approved amendments to CST's organizing statute at its session of 24 Dec 2024 (matching Resolution 430's date) without reproducing article-level text. eastlaws.com's search snippet independently confirms Resolution 430's number, exact date (23/6/1446H), and exact Umm Al-Qura Gazette issue number and date (5065, 17/7/1446H) but its own page returned HTTP 403 to both curl and WebFetch (subscription-gated). almirkaz.com's directory listing likewise confirms the decree's existence/number/date but is subscription-gated beyond that (confirmed via a direct fetch returning 'ليس لديك الصلاحيات للإطلاع على التفاصيل'). A direct attempt to locate the underlying Umm Al-Qura Gazette issue (5065) on uqn.gov.sa itself (reachable, HTTP 200) was not completed to full success within this pass's time budget -- the site's own archive-by-issue-number navigation was not resolved to the specific issue this pass; this is flagged as an avenue for a future pass to strengthen the Articles 1/5/8/10 tier further, not silently omitted.

STRUCTURE: flat sequence of 19 individually-numbered مواد, no أبواب/فصول subdivision, no inline per-article titles in the source (every heading is a bare ordinal followed by a colon) -- no title_ar key is used, consistent with this corpus's rega_organizational_statute/saudi_engineers_law/tvtc_organizational_statute precedent.

SIX ARTICLES CARRY CONFIRMED, SAFELY-RECONSTRUCTABLE AMENDMENTS: Article 1 (one definition deleted, one added -- Resolution 430); Article 3 (complete substitution, 26 functions -- Resolution 430, chained after a since-fully-superseded Resolution 133 renaming/IT-tasks addition); Article 4 (complete substitution, 7-member board -- Resolution 430, chained after a since-fully-superseded Resolution 120 partial paragraph-1-only substitution); Article 5 (two paragraphs replaced, one paragraph deleted, one closing paragraph added -- Resolution 430); Article 8 (three new paragraphs appended -- Resolution 430); Article 10 (complete substitution, 8 financial-resource items -- Resolution 430). Every one of these is a clean, fully-specified instruction (exact paragraph letter/number named, or a complete 'لتكون بالنص الآتي' substitution) -- none required this track to invent an unstated insertion point, EXCEPT Article 1's new 'القطاعات ذات الصلة بالهيئة' definition, whose position within the list Resolution 430 does not specify (placed last, flagged).

No legal text is altered beyond whitespace/diacritic normalization (unifying the sources' inconsistent use of 'أ - '/'أ – '/'أ- ' hyphen styles to a single 'أ- ' convention, matching this corpus's rega_organizational_statute precedent) and splicing each amendment decree's own quoted replacement/addition text into the position its own operative clause specifies. Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English text in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en is for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: BOE's own laws.boe.gov.sa page for this statute (confirmed via its most recent Wayback capture, 20260227062514, over a year after Resolution 430 was published in the Umm Al-Qura Gazette) carries a per-article 'تعديلات المادة' amendment-history popup ONLY for Article 3 and Article 4. No such popup exists for Article 1, 5, 8, or 10, even though qanoonsa.com's full reproduction of Resolution 430 explicitly states all four were also amended by that same resolution. This is a confirmed, searched-for-and-absent gap in BOE's own database as of this pass, not an oversight of this research pass -- the CURRENT (post-2024) text of these four articles therefore rests on qanoonsa.com's gazette reproduction alone, with no primary-source (BOE) confirmation yet available. A future pass should re-check BOE's page once it catches up.

Article 1's own definitions of 'التنظيم' ('تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات السعودية'), 'الهيئة' ('هيئة الاتصالات السعودية'), 'المجلس', 'المحافظ', and 'العضو' all still read, verbatim, the Authority's ORIGINAL 2001 name -- not even the intermediate 'هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات' (CITC) name adopted by Resolution 133/1424H, let alone the current 'هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية' (CST) name adopted by Resolution 253/1444H. Likewise 'الوزارة' ('وزارة البرق والبريد والهاتف') and 'الوزير' still read the Ministry's own original, long-superseded name. NEITHER Resolution 133 NOR Resolution 253 NOR Resolution 430 (which explicitly touched Article 1 to delete/add OTHER definitions) contains an instruction textually updating these specific definition lines. This is a CONFIRMED textual inconsistency read directly from the amendment instruments actually found this pass, not an inference -- reported as-is per this corpus's rega_organizational_statute precedent (Article 1's 'وزير الإسكان'), rather than silently harmonized to the Authority's current name.

Both of the Authority's two renaming decisions (Resolution 133/1424H, renaming to 'هيئة الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات'; and Resolution 253/1444H, renaming to 'هيئة الاتصالات والفضاء والتقنية') are broader Council of Ministers naming/mandate decisions rather than textual amendments to specific numbered articles of Resolution 74's own organizing statute -- neither contains a 'wherever the phrase X appears in this statute, substitute Y' instruction. This explains why BOE's own page updates its title/system_title metadata to the current name while the numbered articles' own text (except where independently touched by Resolution 430) remains textually unchanged. This track does not fabricate a textual substitution that no amendment instrument actually contains.

Resolution 430's own recital lists two additional Council of Ministers resolutions -- No. (524), dated 11/9/1443H, and No. (681), dated 29/11/1443H -- alongside Resolution 120 as governing the Board's composition/continuity, and Resolution 430's own operative text (item 2 under 'سادساً') states the then-existing Board (issued under Resolutions 120, 524 and 681) continues in office until a new Board is formed under the now-amended Article 4. This track did NOT independently locate or read Resolutions 524 or 681's own full text this pass (only their existence, numbers, and dates as cited within Resolution 430's own recital) -- since Article 4 has since been fully superseded by Resolution 430's own complete replacement, this does not affect the article's CURRENT text, but is flagged for completeness and as a candidate for a future pass.

Resolution 430 deletes paragraph (ط) from Article 5 (the original committee-forming power, 'تشكيل اللجان وتخويلها الصلاحيات اللازمة لإنجاز المهام المناطة بها') without renumbering/relettering the paragraphs that followed it (ي، ك). This track preserves the resulting letter gap (ح، [ط missing], ي، ك) literally, exactly as the amendment's own text specifies, rather than silently relettering the remaining paragraphs to close the gap.

Resolution 430's instruction adding the 'القطاعات ذات الصلة بالهيئة' definition to Article 1 does not specify where in the list of definitions it should be inserted (unlike its paragraph-lettered instructions elsewhere, e.g. Article 5's 'الفقرة (ب)'). This track places it last, following the original definitions in their existing order, consistent with this corpus's rega_organizational_statute precedent for unpositioned additions -- flagged rather than silently decided.

The base Resolution 74's own recital cites only a Royal Diwan referral transmitting the then-Minister of Post, Telegraph & Telephone's proposal for 'مشروع نظام الاتصالات ومشروع تنظيم هيئة الاتصالات السعودية', plus two PRE-EXISTING tariff regulations (Telex services tariff, Resolution 123/1416H; automatic-telephone tariff, Resolution 517/1393H) that are reviewed but not named as a repealed predecessor ORGANIZING statute. No named predecessor organizational statute was found -- consistent with the Saudi Communications Authority being newly created as an independent legal entity by this same resolution in 1422H/2001G (the telecom sector was previously run directly by the Ministry of Post, Telegraph & Telephone, not by a separate statutory authority).

Both laws.boe.gov.sa and cst.gov.sa returned a TLS connection reset during the handshake itself (CONNECT tunnel completed at HTTP 200, reset during the ClientHello/handshake) on every direct attempt this pass -- confirmed via curl -v traces, not merely a timeout or a generic failure. This matches the prior research pass's finding for laws.boe.gov.sa. UNLIKE that prior pass, however, the Wayback Machine was fully reachable this pass (no egress block, no TLS reset against web.archive.org itself), which is what allowed this track to be built at all -- a fresh attempt in a future pass may find laws.boe.gov.sa itself live again, at which point its own per-article popups for Articles 1, 5, 8, 10 should be re-checked.

nezams.com's own page for this statute has not been updated past Resolution 120 (1440H) -- its own metadata literally states 'التعديلات: لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' outside of the Resolution-120 note embedded in Article 4's text, and its page title/heading still reads the Authority's original 2001 name. nezams.com is used in this track ONLY to triple-corroborate the base (2001) text and to fill Resolution 120's decree number (which BOE's own popup left blank) -- it does NOT corroborate or contradict Resolution 253 or Resolution 430, and must not be read as having reviewed either.

Resolution 430's own operative text (item 2 under 'سادساً', following its complete replacement of Article 10) contains a TRANSITIONAL provision of the AMENDING DECREE itself -- not a new numbered article of the statute -- stating that the Board as constituted under Resolutions 120/524/681 continues in office until a new Board is formed under the amended Article 4. This track does not fabricate a new statute article to carry this transitional/procedural content; it is noted here and in Article 4's own amendment_history for context only.
